note: Hand-written (phase 5 design 5.4; BM-73, BM-75, BM-84, PL-17), its expected results worked out by hand from the version each case edits, and each one checked, before it was written, with phase 4's validate, versionProblems (against every earlier version, with the case's renames) and checkFile. A team edits one of its note types through fixed operations on its newest resolved definition, never by writing one. The readers are packages/forms/test/edit.test.ts and apps/mobile/test/forms/note_type_edit_test.dart (NoteTypeDef.fromJson reads every result, since the phone refuses a whole list naming a version it cannot read, D84). `definitions` holds every resolved definition the cases name, by "<key>@<version>". Each case of `cases` names the note type it edits (`key`), every version of it oldest first (`versions`, the newest last: what the operations change), the team's other active note types each at its current version (`team`), and the platform's, each at its newest released version (`platform`). applyNoteTypeEdits(ops, {versions, team, platform}) in packages/forms/src/edit.ts must answer `expected`: {definition, renames}, the next version (key the type's, version one more than the newest) with the renames versionProblems is to be given, or {refused: {opIndex, code}}, the first operation refused and why. editNoteTypes({key, edits: ops, team: {each team key: its versions}, platform}) in packages/forms/src/edit-fanout.ts must answer the same for these cases, as {published: [that one]}: none of them reaches another note type. Each case of `fanout` is an option operation, or a publish holding one, that rule 5 carries along mapsTo; its `team` gives every version of each of the team's active note types, oldest first, by key, and editNoteTypes must answer `expected`: {published: [{key, definition, renames}]}, the edited note type first and then each other one it changed, by key, or {refused: {opIndex, code, noteTypeKey}}, naming the note type whose field refused it. An operation is {op, ...}: rename_type {title}; set_hidden {path, hidden} (a path is a field's path without an entry part, or a section's id; shown copies the part back, unchanged, from the last version that had it, after the part it followed there); rename_label {path, label} (a field's label, or a section's title); add_option {path, label} (at the end); rename_option {path, code, label}; retire_option {path, code}; move_option {path, code, before} (just before `before`, or at the end when it is null, or in a field it reaches that lacks `before`); add_field {sectionId, kind, label, ...} (at the end of the section; text {lines, maxLength}, choice {many, options: labels}, number {min, max, decimals, unit}); add_section {title, afterSectionId, fields} (null puts it first; a section holds a field from the start); copy_section {fromKey, sectionId, afterSectionId} (from the platform's newest released version when the platform ships fromKey, else from the team's current version of it). The refusal codes: protected (edit-protected.ts: every part of an auto note type; a field with required or noNormal; a section with needs; a field of kind action, problem, photo or info; an option marked exclusive, normal, unable, other, suggests or sensitiveExam, and every option of a protected field; hiding a section or group holding a protected field); in_use (a hide of what a condition, a grid's pickedIn, a flag's clears or another note type's mapsTo names, and a retire of an option a condition asks for); not_found; title_invalid (a type's title empty, only spaces, or over 80 characters); label_invalid (a label or a section's title the schema's text refuses); last_option, last_field, last_section; too_many_fields and too_many_sections (over 40 fields, or 10 sections, whose id the server made, section 11 row 39); not_copyable (another kinds, group, sensitivity, quick or auto, or a section with needs); id_taken (a copied section's id used in any version of the target, or a made id or code in it used anywhere in one); invalid (a copy the validator refuses, and a number field added whose range holds no value at its decimals). An id or a code the server makes is t_ and the lowest number above every t_<n> id and code in any version of the note types the operation changes (rule 3), so a hidden field's and a retired option's are never made again, and one new code is the same in every field an option operation reaches. A field, a section or an option an operation makes carries no mark (rule 1). Renames are those versionProblems reads: a field's at its own path, an option's at each path its answers are stored at (each side of a field with sides); a section's title and a group's label yield none; two renames of one label are one, from the first label to the last, and one back to the label it had, or of a part the publish then hides, is none. `pins` says which operation, refusal, rule (1 to 5) and mark each case holds. Every name, label and title is made up.
